source: M. Drela, Lab 11 Notes - Basic Aircraft Design Rules, MIT 16.Unified, 16 Apr 2009

rules.title: Static margin (design target)
rules.below: Approaches the neutral point. A negative S.M. is unstable in pitch to some degree and makes the aircraft difficult or even impossible to fly.
rules.above: A large S.M. gives large (and annoying) pitch trim changes with changing airspeed and degrades the pitch trim authority of the elevator.
rules.note: The same rule as static-margin-measured, applied to the design target SM_target: it judges whether the designer's choice is plausible, not a measured margin.

rules.title: Static margin (given CG)
rules.below: Approaches the neutral point. A negative S.M. is unstable in pitch to some degree and makes the aircraft difficult or even impossible to fly.
rules.above: A large S.M. gives large (and annoying) pitch trim changes with changing airspeed and degrades the pitch trim authority of the elevator.
rules.note: The same rule as static-margin-design, applied to the margin of a given CG (an existing aircraft, a measured or plan CG). Not available when no CG is supplied.

rules.title: Horizontal tail volume
rules.below: Pitch behaviour is very sensitive to the CG location, the aircraft resists gusts and other upsets poorly and generally wanders in pitch attitude, which makes precise pitch control difficult.
rules.note: Drela's V_h = S_h * l_h / (S * c) uses c = S/b and the arm from the CG; the canon quantity (#1273) uses c_MAC and the arm from the design CG (#1272).

rules.title: Vertical tail volume
rules.below: The aircraft tends to oscillate or wallow in yaw (Dutch roll) as the pilot gives rudder or aileron inputs, which makes precise directional control difficult; poor rudder roll authority in an aircraft that turns with the rudder only.
rules.note: Until #1272 the canon arm is l_V,25 (from the wing quarter-chord MAC), not Drela's arm from the CG.

rules.title: Spiral stability

levels.meaning: A small amount of spiral instability (B = 3...4, say) does not cause major difficulties for an experienced pilot.

rules.below: B < 5 is spirally unstable and B = 5 spirally neutral. Spiral stability is not a hard requirement and most aircraft are spirally unstable, but an RC aircraft that must fly hands-off has to be spirally stable.
rules.note: B = l_V * Gamma / (b * C_L) with Gamma in degrees. Until #1272 the arm is l_V,25.

rules.title: Rudder roll authority (rudder/elevator aircraft)
rules.below: A value of 0.10 will likely give marginal roll control.
rules.above: Costs performance (drag) without adding roll authority. Drela states 0.20 gives very effective control.
rules.above_basis: maintainer 2026-10-25; Drela names no penalty above the range

rules.title: Sideslip in the steady turn (aircraft without ailerons)

levels.meaning: Below the lower end of the typical range of the maximum tolerable sideslip.
Inside the range 5...15 deg that Drela gives for the maximum tolerable sideslip; the limit is difficult to estimate and depends on the aircraft.

rules.above: Flying at a constant nonzero sideslip in the turn can produce a large drag increase if the sideslip is excessive, mainly because the fuselage is partly broadside to the oncoming flow.
rules.note: Drela states beta_turn < (beta_turn)max = 5...15 deg at the tightest expected turn radius. The canon quantity (#1275) is the worst steady turn at phi = 45 deg at the minimum-sink C_L (maintainer, 2026-10-25): a reasoned transfer of Drela's criterion, not a quote.
